articles.title_orig: Silicon Valley plots Jensen Huang’s comeback
articles.title_zh: Silicon Valley plots Jensen Huang’s comeback
articles.content_orig:
In a matter of days, a corporate scandal has toppled the leader of the world’s second-most valuable company, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; thrust his family into the spotlight; raised huge questions about the future of the AI industry; and landed on Washington’s doorstep.
Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday morning in the wake of mounting scrutiny following reports of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom US officials had been investigating as a potential national security risk.
Nvidia’s board named longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Investors and Wall Street analysts are likely to have big questions for her when Nvidia reports its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday.
In the meantime, Jensen Huang and some key members of the Trump administration are facing questions from lawmakers about the sales and transfer of Nvidia chips to China.
Huang has been called to testify in a closed-door congressional hearing on December 1; lawmakers have said they will subpoena him if he doesn’t voluntarily agree to testify. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify next month before the Senate Banking Committee, which has also requested to hear from Huang.
Huang’s resignation represents a rapid and stunning fall from grace for one of the most powerful men in tech. Huang had run and largely been synonymous with Nvidia in the 33 years since he cofounded it in a Denny’s restaurant in 1993.
His Thursday exit was a marked reversal from just days earlier. On Sunday, the Nvidia board said it would investigate whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, but expressed confidence in his leadership and said it did not believe company secrets or national security had been compromised. The same day, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair, but did not name the other party.
But in the subsequent days, growing national security concerns on Capitol Hill — as well as reports that Huang had at least one additional extramarital relationship — appeared to force the board’s hand.
It convened Wednesday night to weigh Huang’s future, and he was out the next morning.
Nvidia’s stock ( NVDA ) has taken a beating amid the scandal. As of Friday’s close, Nvidia’s shares had fallen 12.75% since the start of the week, erasing roughly $573 billion in market value.
That has wider implications beyond just the company and its investors.
Nvidia is one of the largest stocks in the S&P 500 — it comprises about 6% of the total value of the index — meaning its decline has broad implications for many people’s investment and retirement accounts.
CNN’s John Towfighi and Rosa de Acosta contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Samsung might have accidentally shown off Galaxy S27's most eye-catching feature
articles.title_zh: Samsung might have accidentally shown off Galaxy S27's most eye-catching feature
articles.content_orig:
2027 is almost upon us, and it feels like the year disappeared in a puff of smoke. The arrival of the new year also means Samsung’s new Galaxy devices are just around the corner, particularly the anticipated Galaxy S27 series .
After a whirlwind of leaks, the flagship range has seemingly surfaced again, this time courtesy of Samsung itself. Even more exciting, the fresh leaks hint at which color variants are headed to the Galaxy S27 lineup .
If you’ve been following along, you know the Galaxy S27 will be offered in new colorways, which is the usual flair Samsung brings to every flagship series every year. And what better way to reveal it prematurely? Through a set of wallpapers.
These new wallpapers were discovered inside one of the new One UI builds by folks at SammyGuru . As seen in the set shared, it packs five abstract wallpapers with a twisting strip in monochromatic palettes.
These don’t hint at anything obvious with a “27” or “7” shape, but they are very Samsung-ish.
What’s interesting is the choice of shades. These come in deep or navy blue, light blue, white, light pink, and red or burgundy.
Coincidentally, four of these colors were said to be variants of the Galaxy S27 Ultra, according to the prolific leakster IceUniverse over a month ago, with burgundy not included.
However, we can expect Samsung to offer exclusive colorways available only in its Samsung Store. One of those is black or graphite, which was not included. But there will likely be other shades as well.
So what can we build on this piece? Technically, if these are indeed final wallpaper packs, it does suggest the Galaxy S27 series will be offered in these five shades.
It’s unclear whether the vanilla S27 will share all colorways with the S27 Pro and S27 Ultra , but given that the current S26 series shares the same colors across all models, that could likely be the case next year.
Among the palettes, red or burgundy appears to be the new primary coat here, replacing the cobalt violet in the Galaxy S26.
The new color will match a new design for the Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro. The duo is shown in renders with a new back panel and a wide rectangular camera island, mirroring the iPhone 18 Pro’s layout.
Meanwhile, the base Galaxy S26 could keep the same familiar look, with a floating camera lens in a vertical array on the back panel.
Samsung is reportedly planning to unveil the Galaxy S27 earlier than usual, with industry chatter pointing to late January or early February 2027.
The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is the top-tier flagship in 2026. It packs a new built-in privacy display and a sleeker design. It's now on sale at major retailers.

articles.title_zh: Pixel 11 Pro’s HiLight feature also now works on WhatsApp messages
articles.content_orig:
After being barebones at launch, Google is improving on Pixel 11 Pro’s Hilight feature with message support, now including WhatsApp.
As a part of the November 2026 Pixel Drop that was released this week , Google Messages added support for HiLight on the Pixel 11 Pro series. As we reported back in September when Google started beta testing the functionality, users can select a contact and enable a specific color light for phone calls and/or messages.
Google’s announcement only officially introduced support for the Google Messages app but, as it turns out, WhatsApp is also supported.
Shenaz Zack, Senior Director of Product Management over Pixel, confirmed through a brief video on Twitter/X that WhatsApp messages can also now activate HiLight. This isn’t a huge surprise given WhatsApp calls have been supported since day one, but it’s a nice addition for the many users who prefer WhatsApp over SMS/RCS.

articles.title_orig: GTA 6 PS5 Codes Potentially Being Stolen from Physical Copies Using Flashlight Trick
articles.title_zh: GTA 6 PS5 Codes Potentially Being Stolen from Physical Copies Using Flashlight Trick
articles.content_orig:
A potentially problematic manufacturing oversight may be resulting in some GTA 6 codes being stolen from retail PS5 cases.
Some reports claim that by pointing a strong flashlight at the side of the case, it’s possible to shine light into the empty Blu-ray box in such a way that it makes the code printed on the insert visible.
Remember, GTA 6’s physical release is a code-in-box, and doesn’t have a Blu-ray disc.
There is some debate about whether the included poster insert blocks the light and makes this impossible; some say they’ve been able to replicate the issue, while others say it can’t be done with a sealed copy.
It’s also worth noting that the US release specifically has a camouflaged pattern around the code, as shown by ResetEra user Mattmo831. That means you can certainly shine light into the box, but you can’t read the code on the other side.
Some PEGI units don’t have the camouflage pattern, so technically the code is visible using this trick, although again there’s still debate over whether the poster blocks the light in sealed copies.
It’s worth pointing out that codes aren’t activated at the point of purchase like other digital vouchers, so assuming the flashlight method works, it would be perfectly possible to pilfer a working copy of the game.
I think this story will explode if it turns out to be true, but it all just depends on how many PEGI copies don’t have the camouflage pattern and whether the inserted poster blocks the light or not.
As far as I can see, there aren’t an enormous number of people who’ve complained upon buying the physical version that their code has been redeemed – but if this method works, the publicity around it will now surely see the probability increase.

articles.title_orig: Rubio says further US military action is not needed against economically weakened Iran
articles.title_zh: Rubio says further US military action is not needed against economically weakened Iran
articles.content_orig:
President Trump says he is leaning toward a new solution to the Iran nuclear crisis: Declare it is over, even if not much has changed.
Mr. Trump and his team have taken to asserting that they have the Iranians right where they want them. They say they no longer need a new nuclear agreement that would remove potential bomb fuel from the country, or to limit Iran’s missile capability, two of the leading reasons the president cited 10 months ago for going to war.
Mr. Trump appears — at least for now — to have rejected a series of military options that would involve intense, if time-limited, attacks on military installations, nuclear sites and even some energy infrastructure.
All the talk this year of sending in commandos to seize roughly 970 pounds of uranium from the country, enriched to a near-bomb-grade level of 60 percent purity, has been abandoned, albeit for the moment. So has the detailed analysis of whether America’s biggest bunker busters are powerful enough to get deep into Pickaxe Mountain, a site U.S. intelligence believes — but is not sure — is the location of advanced centrifuges that can purify uranium into bomb fuel.
In comments to reporters this week in Paris, where he was attending a meeting of foreign ministers from the Group of 7, Secretary of State Marco Rubio described an approach best characterized as strategic patience: waiting for sanctions on Iran to take their toll and ultimately crack their government.
“At this point, the economic campaign and the pressure and the devastation that our economic campaign is having on the Iranian regime is working so well that the president really doesn’t have any need to conduct major combat operations,” Mr. Rubio said.

articles.title_orig: Bay Area Denny's takes down plaque commemorating Jensen Huang
articles.title_zh: Bay Area Denny's takes down plaque commemorating Jensen Huang
articles.content_orig:
Amidst the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the original Denny’s location where he once worked removed the plaque that celebrated his success.
Amidst the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the original Denny's location where he once worked removed the plaque that celebrated his success. On Friday, the restaurant announced it was reinstalling it.
The plaque was presented on Sept. 26, 2023 , by the CEO of Denny's, Kelli Valade, highlighting the very booth Huang conceived his idea for Nvidia. The plaque was removed as of Thursday, but on Friday, the company announced it was reinstalling it.
Watch NBC Bay Area News free wherever you are
Denny’s released the following statement on the matter:
“We’re reinstalling the plaque recognizing the conversations at Denny’s that helped launch NVIDIA.
Jensen Huang started at Denny’s as a dishwasher. Years later, he and his co-founders gathered in one of our booths to discuss the idea that became NVIDIA. The plaque commemorates that shared history. America’s Diner has long been a place where people and ideas come together, and that history deserves to be preserved.”
On Thursday, Huang resigned from his duties at Nvidia. On the same day, Nvidia shares fell by more than 4%, according to the Associated Press.
The New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman suspected to be a Chinese spy by U.S. Intelligence. On Sunday, Nvidia said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised by this affair.
Still, lawmakers in Washington D.C. are calling for further investigations on the matter. President Donald Trump confirmed the FBI is looking into the affair.

articles.title_orig: Afghanistan’s new road to China ends at a closed border
articles.title_zh: Afghanistan’s new road to China ends at a closed border
articles.content_orig:
At an altitude of nearly 4,900 metres, at the Wakhjir Pass, Afghanistan ends and China begins. Snow closes the pass for at least five months of the year, and people cross it only sporadically in the months when it is passable.
There is no official border crossing here, and yet, on October 4, Afghanistan’s Taliban-led government celebrated the opening of a road leading to the frontier – but crucially not crossing it.
Afghanistan’s Ministry of Rural Rehabilitation and Development said the road through the Wakhan Corridor in Badakhshan province had been built in two phases for 365 million afghanis ($5.5m).
It is a basic road – an unpaved track covered with gravel. On the other side of the border, there is no Chinese customs facility, and China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has not commented on the road’s opening.
For the moment, the road leads to a closed border, with no indication of when Beijing might open it to commercial traffic.
The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow protruding stretch of land extending for about 350 kilometres (220 miles). It lies between Tajikistan to the north and Pakistan to the south, but is entirely within Afghan territory, connecting it with China.
The corridor’s unusual shape was determined by the competition between Britain and Russia over the region in the 19th century. An agreement between the two powers in 1895 delineated Afghanistan’s northern boundary with Russian territories (that now make up modern-day Tajikistan), and left Wakhan under Kabul’s control to separate the Russian-controlled land from British India.
China was not a party to the conflict, however, and Kabul and Beijing did not settle the border until 1963.
The area – on both sides of the border – is remote. But in recent years it has gradually become one of Asia’s most sensitive geopolitical crossroads, where China’s security concerns, Afghanistan’s economic ambitions, the interests of Pakistan and Iran, and Central Asian countries’ regional connectivity projects intersect.
As competition intensifies over trade and logistics routes across Asia, this narrow corridor could take on a role far beyond its geographical limits: a potential link between South, East and Central Asia, and a key to reshaping patterns of trade and influence in the region.
Serious discussion of a road through Wakhan began in June 2009, during discussions between the Afghan and Chinese governments.
However, the project went no further than preliminary studies at the time, with the corridor’s rugged terrain cited as a major obstacle to implementation.
The Chinese press at the time also noted concerns over national security, particularly that Uighur fighters could use the corridor as an entry point into China.
The project was frozen until 2019, when Afghanistan began building a road in Wakhan, according to former Afghan ambassador to China, Javid Qaem.
Sixty kilometres (37 miles) were completed, “but the sudden change of government in Afghanistan in August 2021 led to the plan being postponed”, Qaem told Al Jazeera, in reference to the Taliban takeover.
Former Afghan acting defence minister, Shah Mahmoud Miakhel, who served in the position in 2021 and left a few months before the Taliban took power, told Al Jazeera that “the presence of [United States] and foreign forces and the security situation” prevented the road project from being implemented.
“Beijing considered those circumstances to be limiting the prospects for developing the corridor,” Miakhel said.
The Taliban government, however, picked up the project in the years since, making it one of its strategic projects while strengthening political and diplomatic contacts with Beijing.
It hopes to turn the corridor from an isolated border area into a gateway connecting Afghanistan to Chinese and Central Asian markets and strengthening its position in regional trade networks.
“The Taliban resumed construction of the Wakhan road in September 2023, seeking financial support from China to build this future trade route, but China has not yet agreed to open its border with Afghanistan because of security threats,” Qaem said.
In January 2024, the Taliban announced that the road had reached the Chinese border. In March 2025, the rural development ministry signed a contract with local companies for a second, 71-kilometre (44-mile) phase. The authorities say the project was funded from Afghan government resources, and the available information does not indicate any Chinese funding.
In August 2025, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi – the most senior Chinese official to visit Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power – made his second visit to Kabul since the takeover.
In his meeting with Afghan Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani, Wang said China “supports the early resumption of bilateral patrols in the Wakhan Corridor to maintain peace and tranquillity in the border areas”. He also called on Kabul to crack down on the East Turkestan Islamic Movement, a Uighur separatist group.
Unlike Afghanistan, China does not view the Wakhan Corridor primarily as an economic project, but as a highly sensitive security issue. Beijing’s priorities in Afghanistan fall into three main areas: protecting its western border, preventing armed groups from entering Xinjiang (East Turkestan), and safeguarding its investments in natural resources, as well as protecting the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.
An Afghan government source, who requested anonymity, offered Kabul’s account of China’s position.
“China does not oppose opening its border with Afghanistan through the Wakhan Corridor, but it links implementation of the project to the availability of effective security guarantees,” the source told Al Jazeera. The source said that the Taliban had demonstrated their ability to maintain security and secure the border.
The question of Xinjiang, considered by the Uighur people to be their homeland, is therefore the apparent priority for China when it comes to Wakhan.
A 2022 United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights report condemned the “arbitrary detention of Uighurs and other Muslims in Xinjiang”. China has rejected the findings, describing them as part of a Western campaign against it.
Beijing continues to proceed cautiously when it comes to Afghanistan. Major Chinese investments have stalled. In June 2025, the Taliban cancelled an oil exploration contract in the Amu Darya Basin with a Chinese company, saying it had failed to fulfil its obligations. And in May of this year, Afghanistan’s mining minister complained to the Chinese ambassador about delays in the Mes Aynak copper mine project, which has yet to begin production.
China shares land borders with 14 countries and maintains extensive economic and trade relations with most of its neighbours. But Afghanistan, alongside Bhutan, remain the only countries bordering China that have yet to benefit from a direct overland crossing for trade.
Kabul wants Wakhan to provide a route that is not controlled by Islamabad. Afghanistan is landlocked, and its routes to the sea run through Pakistan and Iran. Over the past year, both routes have been all but closed at the same time.
Mohammad Ismail Ghaznawi, who was governor of Badakhshan before becoming deputy minister of public works for road maintenance in August, said the Wakhan road project was “part of the government’s plan to diversify trade outlets and reduce dependence on Pakistani border crossings”, and referenced fighting between Afghan and Pakistani forces that has been ongoing this year.
Ghaznawi added that the US-Israel war on Iran also directly affects Afghan trade, making the opening of alternative routes a priority.
The Afghan government views the road as the beginning of a trade corridor, and perhaps a railway in the future, that would connect the country to China’s Belt and Road Initiative and generate transit fees.

articles.title_orig: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
articles.title_zh: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
articles.content_orig:
In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass.
Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant. His family had been killed by the poachers who took him.
More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary – but he still lives alone. He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends.
Jojo's carers at the Lekedi Foundation in Gabon want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla – that Jojo could live and bond with. But finding him a friend - and bringing them into his life - is not straightforward.
"He's probably the most extreme case of isolation I've ever seen in a great ape," says Prof Gillian Forrester from the University of Sussex, who is studying Jojo as part of research into great ape psychology and how to help rescued animals recover from trauma.
Jojo was less than a year old – an infant clinging to his mother – when he was captured and sold.
Most gorillas spend the first 14 to 19 years of their life in an embedded family unit but he was kept completely alone and on public display at the private zoo that bought him.
Maxe Anaclet Makaba, who is head keeper at Lekedi and sees Jojo nearly every day, says it is clear he "craves human interaction".
"He will even go to the trouble of gathering leaves for us to hold, so that we [trade them] for a treat – to interact with us," he says.
Jojo also calls out when women he knows well visit his enclosure and then leave, making sounds that silverback males use to summon the females in the wild, explains Éric Willaume, who runs the sanctuary.
"He definitely feels lonely," he says.
Jojo is one of the more than 6,000 African primates estimated to have been bought or sold in the global trade of apes and other primates between 2000 and 2023. Thousands more are trafficked illegally for use as exotic pets, wild meat, and traditional medicine, the Pan African Sanctuary Alliance says.
Experts believe when baby great apes are taken from their group at a young age like Jojo, they are left traumatised.
"If they're old enough to understand what happened to them, to understand their family was killed, they just lose the will to live," explains conservationist Tony King, from UK charity the Aspinall Foundation. "You see it in their eyes – the light goes out. I never knew where that expression came from, but I've seen it in gorillas."
King – who specialises in rehabilitating rescued great apes – remembers rescuing two infant sister gorillas who were brought to a sanctuary in the Congo Basin.
"They were clinging to each other," he says. "They stayed together in a little tight ball for about three days before they sort of unravelled. I think that's what kept them alive."
African charity the Gorilla Rehabilitation and Conservation Education (Grace) Center uses what it calls "gorilla-led" rehabilitation. When the team rescues a young gorilla from the pet trade, they put it with a group as soon as possible so they can socialise and essentially learn to be a gorilla.
But Jojo's case is unusual. He is fully mature and showing signs of harmful, chronic stress, according to Forrester.
In a game-changing approach to studying anxiety and trauma in apes, she has used a thermal camera to film Jojo's face. This allows her to monitor blood flow, revealing what appears to be a chronically cold nose.
It's a sign of a malfunctioning stress response. When any primate – a human, chimp or gorilla - is stressed, blood flow to the eyes and ears increases. It puts them on high alert for danger, but leaves their nose, temporarily, colder. For Jojo, this "nasal dip" as it is known, does not seem to recover.
"Being connected to others is incredibly important to our psychology as great apes," Forrester says. "Having another individual to share his life with would be so healing for him.
"I would assume other gorillas would help him process this grief and trauma."
Dr Katie Fawcett, from the Grace Center, says it's also "essential" for an animal to form social relationships to be considered for release into the wild - which is the ultimate goal for Jojo's keepers.
The bonds between gorillas – what we would call friendship - is key to their society, adds Dr Robin Morrison from the University of Zurich, who studies the social lives of mountain gorillas. In one recent study, she discovered that female mountain gorillas would seek out females they knew, even if they hadn't seen them for many years, when joining a group.
And she says a big part of a gorilla's normal social life is "just sitting together quietly sharing space".
But Jojo has never been given the opportunity to sit quietly with another gorilla.
No one knows how Jojo will react to a companion. Moving an animal from an accredited zoo would be a decision for an international committee and based on genetics, health and the animals' personalities and compatibility.
Any introduction to another animal would be done very carefully – perhaps giving them an object that smells of the other before they see each other.
These slow, cautious ape introductions do happen – when an animal moves from one zoo group to another, for example. Forrester has contacted a number of accredited zoos to explore the possibility of doing this for Jojo. But those discussions have fizzled out with no sign of progress.
The problem, she says, is "there aren't clear processes in place to do these kinds of trans-locations".
The international rules and processes for moving captive gorillas across international borders - from one zoo or safari park to another - are designed for breeding programmes.
"They're not designed for reintroductions into the wild, or to find companions for animals that might need them," says Forrester.
And because Jojo, who is probably in his 20s, has reached maturity, King thinks it might be too late for him to bond with other gorillas.
"Jojo's situation is unique, but he is probably best where he is," King says, adding that introducing him to another animal could, somewhat ironically, be a source of more stress for him.
Being alone is also natural, even relatively common, for mature male gorillas. According to Morrison, about a third of adult males are solitary. "When they reach adolescence, they tend to disperse and spend a good chunk of their life on their own."
Solo males will try to persuade females to form a group with them, but some don't succeed and may feel lonely as a consequence, Morrison believes. "If we think of loneliness in an evolutionary context - this mismatch between the social interactions they want and the social interactions they're getting. I suspect feeling lonely is part of the natural, evolutionary drive to attract females."
But while those phases – of family life and adult solitude - play a role in wild gorilla society, Jojo was forced into solitary confinement as an infant.
Morrison believes Jojo is probably both traumatised and lonely.
"[In the wild] gorillas move together, find food together, sleep together," she says. "So much of their lives is just being with this group."
That is what Jojo's keepers, Forrester, and others want for Jojo. A friend. Maybe a female, or a compatible male.
"It would be good for him to have a companion," says keeper Makaba. "Because being alone is like being cut off from the world - it's like being in prison.
"Having another gorilla there would be a good thing for him."

articles.title_zh: Metaphor: ReFantazio Switch 2 Patch To Resolve Colour Glitch
articles.content_orig:
Metaphor: ReFantazio arrived on the Switch 2 this week, and while the port has been well-received by fans and critics alike, there's one issue you may encounter.
Sega (and Atlus) have acknowledged this an official Japanese post about the game's release. Fortunately, it's not a game-breaking bug or anything like that, it just changes the colours of objects and characters. Here's a rough translation:
Atlus: "We have confirmed that after playing for a certain period, some objects and characters temporarily display colors different from their original colors. This bug does not affect game progress.
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 855k
"We are preparing an update patch to fix this bug. When the stream begins, we will announce it on the official X account and official website."
As noted, a patch to address this issue is already in the works. This bug apparently can appear after 30 hours of gameplay.
Alongside this news, Atlus has also shared a special illustration to commemorate the release of this title on the Switch 2 this week. The artwork is from the game's character designer Shigenori Soejima.
If you aren't already playing this game on the Switch 2, there's a demo you can download from the eShop (save data also carries over), and you can find out more information about this version of the title in our review here on Nintendo Life.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market News, Nov. 13, 2026: Nvidia Shares Drop Again as Investors Eye Fallout From Huang's Removal
articles.title_zh: Stock Market News, Nov. 13, 2026: Nvidia Shares Drop Again as Investors Eye Fallout From Huang's Removal
articles.content_orig:
The Nasdaq Composite fell on Friday as Nvidia shares added to their recent losses, though the index still notched a winning week alongside the other two major averages.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq dropped 0.91% to 25,136.27, while the S&P 500 slid 0.4% to 7,561.67. The Dow Jones Industrial Average eked out a gain of 50.46 points, or 0.1%, to end at 52,347.55.
Equities initially popped after October's producer price index reading — a measure of wholesale inflation — showed an increase of 0.3% on the month. Economists polled by Dow Jones had seen headline PPI rising 0.4%.
However, the report also showed producer prices gaining 6.5% from 12 months earlier — the biggest annual advance since November 2022.
Nvidia shares weighed on the broader market for another day. The stock fell 2% Friday, extending the more than 4% drop it saw in the previous session. The pressure came after the exit of the scandal-hit chipmaker's founder and CEO Jensen Huang.
HSBC downgraded the chipmaker Friday to hold, believing that the stock will languish until the company lays out a permanent succession plan.
Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress , who's worked at the company for more than a decade, will lead the chipmaker as interim CEO. The company's board is looking both internally and externally for a full-time replacement for Huang.
Thomas Martin of Globalt Investments expects the process of finding a new CEO to "take a lot of time" and spur even more uncertainty for the name.
"What will happen to those types of financing arrangements, and will there be less of them just going forward or will there actually be unwinding of them?" the senior portfolio manager told CNBC. "What are the relationships going to be with their suppliers and with their customers? It's just early days."
The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all pulled back on Thursday after Huang stepped down from his post following reported extramarital affairs , including a relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy. Analysts told CNBC that Huang's exit could trigger a 20% correction in the stock.
To be sure, Baird's Ross Mayfield believes a lot of pain has already been priced into the stock, though he still anticipates volatility ahead. More broadly, he expects to see investors continue to rotate into non-AI corners of the market independent of the latest developments with Nvidia.
"Even before all of this came out, and even before the election, chip stocks had been under pressure. There had already been worries about a blue wave — worries about a Democratic sweep — [and] worries about the [return on investment] on all of this capex," the investment strategist said. "It hasn't really changed the broad tenor of the market."
Even with the latest bout of market turbulence, the major averages notched weekly advances. The Nasdaq added 2.3%, while the S&P 500 rose 2.5%. The Dow gained 2.1%. All three indexes scored their best weekly performances since early August.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite finished in negative territory on Friday.
The broad market index fell 0.4% to 7,561.67, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq shed 0.91% to 25,136.27.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed, rising 50.46 points, or 0.1%, to 52,347.55.
Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia is scrambling the tech landscape as investors try to gauge the fallout for chip makers, neoclouds, and others in the artificial intelligence arms race.
The market has quickly passed judgement — bidding up shares of chipmakers like Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom while pushing down neoclouds such as Coreweave and AI server maker Dell Technologies .
Traders can benefit from the volatility, but the market has a tendency to overshoot in both directions and estimates are changing rapidly. Long-term investors may want to wait until the dust settles.
CNBC Pro subscribers can read more here .
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.
Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.
"Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.
Apple shares climbed nearly 1% Friday, reaching an intraday record of $360.80, lifting the company's market value above $5.2 trillion.
The stock has benefited as investors move away from companies exposed to the AI infrastructure boom.
While many of its Magnificent Seven peers are committed to AI infrastructure buildouts, Apple has managed to stay away from the costly AI arms race. Bernstein analysts recently called Apple a "safe haven " and reiterated an outperform rating on Apple in the report, and a $380 price target, implying about 7% upside from Thursday's close.
Check out CNBC's live blog here to read more about the stocks making big moves on Friday.
— Darla Mercado and Ananya Chetia
Cisco topped estimates on fiscal first-quarter earnings on Thursday, but Wall Street analysts are still somewhat measured on the outlook for the make of networking technologies amid the AI boom.
Tim Long at Barclays maintained his equal-weight rating on the stock in a Friday note, with a price target of $109 and potential upside of 6.9%.
"One area of weakness in the quarter was that hyperscaler AI orders were likely down meaningfully Q/Q in FQ1 based on our estimates, but these orders tend to be lumpy," he said.
Michael Ng at Goldman Sachs has a neutral rating on the stock, noting an "orders miss," per a Nov. 12 note.
"The margin outlook and upgrade was better-than-expected with CSCO demonstrating strong operating leverage, though growing hyperscale revenue mix may be headwinds to gross margin in F2H27," he said.
Nvidia is going to struggle until it gets a new CEO to permanently replace Jensen Huang and take over from CFO-turned-interim-CEO Colette Kress, according to HSBC.
Analyst Frank Lee downgraded the chipmaker to hold from buy. His price target of $170, down from $365, implies upside of just 2.3% from Thursday's close.
"We believe the uncertainties will prevail until a permanent succession plan is laid out and the new CEO is able to demonstrate execution capabilities," Lee said in a Friday note to clients.
CNBC Pro subscribers can read more here .
Bitcoin traded below $70,000 for the first time since August in a risk-off move, falling as low as $67,632.68, its lowest level since Aug. 19, according to Coin Metrics.
Its recent weakness coincides with strength in the U.S. dollar. On Friday, the dollar index reached its highest level since April 2025, following hotter-than-expected inflation earlier this week that increased expectations of further Fed tightening, pushing Treasury yields and the dollar higher while pressuring both bitcoin and gold – despite their appeal as alternative stores of value in the longer term.
Throughout November, bitcoin has been struggling from the combination of dollar strength, institutional selling and, this week, more than $1 billion in leveraged bitcoin liquidations, per CoinGlass. The declines began in late October, as concerns over AI valuations and spending fueled a broad tech sell-off, and were compounded by the $6.3 billion Binance hack and weakening institutional ETF demand.

articles.title_orig: Bessent accuses Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia chips
articles.title_zh: Bessent accuses Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia chips
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has reportedly agreed to testify before lawmakers next month as the spotlight on him grows harsher amid Nvidia's ( NVDA ) turmoil.
Both Democrats and Republicans alike are raising questions about whether Lutnick went too far in protecting Nvidia's push to sell its chips overseas even as the US government was warning about a possible security breach.
Lutnick is reportedly set to appear on Dec. 10 before the Senate Banking Committee, in news first reported by Fox News. Spokespersons for the Commerce Department and the Senate panel did not immediately provide additional details.
The appearance would set up what could be a major moment for the suddenly embattled Commerce secretary after days in which he and the White House had largely stayed silent as even some of Trump's closest allies grew more vocal.
Lutnick will appear before Republican Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chairman of the Senate panel until the end of the year and a regular on President Trump's campaign stops last month. Scott released a letter Thursday evening requesting that Lutnick and ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang appear before Congress early next month.
"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology," Scott wrote. "The American people deserve answers."
Republican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana used more colorful language in a recent appearance on CNN , saying he wanted answers about why the Commerce Department allowed Nvidia to sell chips to an alleged Chinese spy's company.
"This whole thing is an intergalactic freak show," Kennedy said.
Some Trump aides have declined to defend Lutnick emphatically.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent raised eyebrows Friday during a CNBC appearance when he reiterated his desire for stronger government limits on advanced semiconductor exports — which he added that the Pentagon, State Department, and the trade representative's office agreed with.
"Commerce has the pen…," Bessent said, "and you will have to ask them about their internal processes."
The rapid-fire developments have also increased the odds of Congress passing new curbs on semiconductor exports to China, with lawmakers now moving to add some combination of three bipartisan plans into a military funding bill that needs to pass before the end of the year.
A White House official said that Trump maintains confidence in Lutnick, but the president's only direct reaction to the scandal in recent days was a Truth Social post saying Huang had "done a fantastic job" and that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over Nvidia.
The administration's response has done little to quell the questions from lawmakers after reports about whether Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy endangered US national security and painted Lutnick as a roadblock in responding, even as other Trump aides pushed for more muscular action.
The New York Times reported that Trump was warned about the possible security issues with Nvidia on two separate occasions but didn't act.
These questions have led to a flurry of calls for investigations and for Lutnick and Huang to testify. Huang has agreed to appear before a House panel before Thanksgiving, though a date hasn't been set yet.
Republican Sen. Jim Banks of Indiana said he wants to hear from Lutnick soon "because we have a lot of bipartisan questions and concerns about what's happened over the last year."
Democrats are set to take control of the House and Senate committees that oversee trade and have already launched an investigation into Lutnick.
The flood of criticism has led senior White House officials to discuss whether Lutnick should be pushed out, according to a Reuters report , but it is not yet clear if Trump is willing to jettison a close ally who has survived other accusations in the first two years of Trump's second term.
This spring, Lutnick was forced to revise his account of his ties to Jeffrey Epstein after the release of the disgraced financier's files revealed that Lutnick had contact with Epstein for years longer than he had previously claimed.
Lutnick was forced to testify before Congress about the matter — and Democrats called it an embarrassing episode — but Trump stood by him.
Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

articles.content_orig:

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his top post at the chipmaker he co-founded, after reports of the tech titan's extramarital affairs came into the spotlight this week.
One of those relationships has raised national security concerns. The New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with a businesswoman U.S. intelligence suspects to be a Chinese spy, which Beijing denies. Separately, the outlet and later others reported that Nvidia employees said Huang had another affair with an executive who reported to him directly — compounding calls for him to step down.
Nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Thursday, effective immediately. The California-based company said that Colette Kress — who has been Nvidia's chief financial officer and executive vice president since 2013 — will step into the role of interim CEO.
The scandal marks the most tumultuous chapter yet for Nvidia, whose high-end chips have emerged as the leading building blocks for artificial intelligence. Huang himself has become a key face in the AI race, both across the industry and often on U.S. President Donald Trump’s side in Washington.
Nvidia said Kress is now interim CEO. Prior to joining Nvidia over 13 years ago, Kress worked at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments.
In a statement about her new post on Thursday, Kress said Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she's “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”
Huang co-founded Nvidia, alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, back in 1993 — and until Thursday had led the company ever since, with no clear successor in sight. Huang's ouster has led to a scramble for a new permanent CEO, and Nvidia said it's considering both “internal and external candidates.”
The company's board of directors also said Thursday that it has named its first-ever chairman, Harvey C. Jones.
Over the weekend, following news reports of Huang's relationship with a woman identified as former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, Nvidia's then-CEO apologized for being “unfaithful to my wife.”
"My actions hurt her and our children,” Huang wrote in a Sunday email to employees, adding that his colleagues also “deserve better” from him.
Neither Huang nor Nvidia identified who he had been intimate with by name, but the apology arrived shortly after Nvidia said it was investigating whether Huang had been “the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
Last month, the Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies discovered Nvidia’s Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, who also goes by the name Huang Le — and determined she was feeding information directly to Beijing. (Huang is a common surname and the two are not related).
Nvidia initially maintained Huang would stay on as CEO as the company conducted its investigation. But scrutiny grew late Wednesday after reports emerged that Huang had a separate affair with an Nvidia executive. Huang’s resignation arrived shortly after. The company didn't address either relationship in its Thursday announcement.
Later on Thursday, Reuters reported Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee, citing unidentified sources.
Where investigations stand
Nvidia hasn't provided any notable new updates in its internal review announced Sunday. At the time, the company said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.
Trump was reportedly briefed about intelligence findings involving Huang well before the scandal erupted publicly. But when asked over the weekend whether he wished he had acted sooner on that information, the president said “I don’t think so” and maintained that Nvidia’s CEO was an “honorable guy.”
Trump later said the FBI is looking into Huang's affair with Alice Huang, although where exactly that probe stands is unclear. Meanwhile, lawmakers from both sides of the aisle on Capitol Hill are calling for further investigations.
Many eyes have been on Nvidia’s ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which prominently touts the companies’ partnership on its website. Last year, Megaspeed was accused of illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports.
On Thursday, Megaspeed maintained it takes its obligation to comply with American export control laws “extremely seriously" — and that it was committed to working “constructively and transparently” with the U.S. government.
Singaporean authorities said they questioned Alice Huang and confiscated her passport last year as part of an investigation into Megaspeed. They concluded there wasn’t enough evidence that she had committed a crime, but suspected she provided “inaccurate information” to downplay her role at Megaspeed.
Malaysia said Friday it was investigating whether any of the chips brought into Malaysia by Megaspeed or its Malaysian affiliate Speedmatrix had been reexported to other country.
China, meanwhile, has denied that it attempted to ensnare Jensen Huang. Its Foreign Ministry earlier this week called the spying allegations “unsubstantiated” and said they amount to a smear campaign against Beijing.
Trump continues his praise for Huang
Huang has maintained a close relationship to Trump throughout the Republican president’s second term in office. He’s successfully lobbied for looser AI regulation overall — including less strict limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. And he's among tech CEOs who have dined at the White House, and even traveled on Air Force One.
Trump has called Huang “smart” and “amazing,” repeatedly insisting he join him on foreign trips. After news of his resignation broke on Thursday, the president maintained that Huang had “done a fantastic job.”
He also chimed in with his own recommendation for Nvidia's CEO seat: former chief executive of Apple Tim Cook, who has similarly remained in Trump's orbit over recent years.
“There is only one man to take his place,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform Thursday. “Legend replaces a Legend!”
Critics quickly decried Trump's comments. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said the Republican administration had “repeatedly undermined the free market economy” and that Thursday marked the latest example of “ Donald Trump weighing in on behalf of his views connected to corporate America, as opposed to focusing on working class America.”
A new test for the AI industry
The shockwaves of Huang's exit stress just how few figures hold so much power the AI race. Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable companies today — and Huang himself (often wearing his signature leather jacket) has risen to fame across the tech world.
Some analysts suspect the foreign intelligence allegations will strengthen calls in Washington for stricter export controls with China, which could in turn renew trade strains overall. Others have called it a watershed moment for Nvidia, the chipmaker that has long been seen as the crown jewel for powering AI. And questions of security risks facing the companies at the forefront of this technology are piling up.
Nvidia shares fell more than 4% by market close Thursday, after plummeting earlier in the day.
Stephanie Balaouras, group research director for Forrester, said Huang’s resignation from Nvidia isn’t just a test for the company but the AI boom as a whole.
“If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience," she said. “If its stock, financing relationships, or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the

articles.title_orig: Super Micro, run by Jensen Huang’s friend, says Megaspeed was ‘never’ its customer
articles.title_zh: Super Micro, run by Jensen Huang’s friend, says Megaspeed was ‘never’ its customer
articles.content_orig:
Super Micro Computer says that Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the center of the spy scandal that brought down Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, has never been one of its customers.
The assertion by Super Micro, whose cofounder was arrested earlier this year on charges of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, comes as observers look for possible connections between two companies whose business dealings with Nvidia are under scrutiny.
“Megaspeed is not, and has never been, a Supermicro customer,” a spokesperson told Fortune in a statement. The company also said it “has been responsive to inquiries and has fully cooperated with U.S. and Taiwanese officials, while also voluntarily providing information and engaging with all requests from Singapore authorities to date.”
Supermicro’s statement came after Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said Thursday that the Singapore Police Force and Customs had opened investigations into Megaspeed and Alice Huang, a former top executive there who had an affair with Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, and who some authorities believe was acting as a spy for China.
Singapore authorities said they had asked Supermicro for information and had received only “limited cooperation.” The ministry said the Supermicro cooperation matter was first raised with U.S. authorities on July 7, 2025 and then repeatedly afterward with the Department of Justice and the FBI.
Alice Huang, who isn’t related to ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, drew intense scrutiny after reports that she and the Nvidia co-founder were having an affair, which came out before his resignation on Wednesday. The U.S. Attorney’s Office in Manhattan is reportedly looking into whether entities linked to her helped smuggle Supermicro hardware with Nvidia GPUs into China. Multiple probes have been initiated into export control breaches related to Alice and her businesses, including Megaspeed. Jensen, Nvidia, and Supermicro have not been charged with wrongdoing.
However, Jensen’s downfall has cast a dark cloud over Supermicro at an intensely complicated moment for the hardware and liquid cooling tech company. One of Supermicro’s three co-founders, Charles Liang, is a longtime friend of Jensen’s and the two both hail from Taiwan. They’ve shared the stage at multiple massive Computex tech events in Taiwan, including in 2024 when Jensen was photographed having drinks with Alice. Both cofounded their companies in 1993 and Supermicro’s close relationship with Nvidia has been a boon for customers hoping to be first in line for the latest generations of high-performing chips Nvidia churns out.
Another Supermicro cofounder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, was arrested and charged in March along with two others for allegedly working to route about $2.5 billion in servers with Nvidia’s H200 and B200 GPUs into China through a Southeast Asian front company. Liaw has pleaded not guilty, and his trial has been pushed to March 2027. A co-defendant, Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, pleaded guilty in October. Supermicro has said it was a victim of the scheme and conducted an internal investigation finding no evidence current members of senior management were aware of the alleged conspiracy. Supermicro’s stock fell nearly 4% this week.
In August, prosecutors in Keelung, Taiwan indicted nine people over 130 Supermicro servers with Nvidia B300 chips that were allegedly cleared for shipment using forged data-center inspection records . Some 74 of the servers made it to China and customs intercepted the rest. The defendants include two former Supermicro Taiwan employees and a former Nvidia Taiwan employee, who face breach of trust and document forgery charges. In Taiwan, unauthorized AI chip exports to China aren’t currently considered a criminal offense, which is why the charges relate to forgery and breach-of-trust charges. Neither Nvidia nor Supermicro was charged.
The company said in a statement that it “maintains a robust compliance program and continues to work closely with authorities and industry partners to combat diversion and help protect American innovation.” The company has disclosed a grand jury subpoena and inquiries from the SEC, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, and foreign authorities.
Amanda Gerut is the west coast editor at Fortune , overseeing publicly traded businesses, executive compensation, Securities and Exchange Commission regulations, and investigations.

articles.title_orig: Why Anthropic’s Dario Amodei Has Angered OpenAI and Other A.I. Peers
articles.title_zh: Why Anthropic’s Dario Amodei Has Angered OpenAI and Other A.I. Peers
articles.content_orig:
Don't bother applying for a job at Anthropic if your goal is to be the star of the show.
That was one of the first things Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei emphasized on Friday, in a live-streamed interview with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon ahead of the AI startup's hotly anticipated IPO . Amodei said the company has been "very disciplined about turning down people who are deeply technically talented," but don't fit its culture. The company's recent IPO filing stated that its workforce grew from about 940 employees at the end of 2024 to about 5,300 as of late September.
"We don't want people who are jerks. We don't want people who try to steal the show and don't work well with others. We don't want people who aren't oriented towards the public benefit," Amodei told Dimon.
Amodei, who worked as vice president of research at research at OpenAI and was a senior research scientist at Google Brain, said talent and culture "are the most important things" for a company. He said he now devotes 40% to 50% of his time to focusing on those priorities.
The CEO said that talent and culture create technology, and the company's presence and how it's viewed by the public comes from the talent and intentions of the people who build that technology. Amodei said he and his six cofounders decided at the company's founding that talent and culture would be their priority.
"If you stick to that consistently, it's painful in the short run. But you get a team where everyone works together, and everyone is on the same side," Amodei said.
Anthropic describes itself as a "high-trust, low-ego organization" on its website, and in its IPO filing said that "teams operate in a truth-seeking environment where the best argument wins, not the loudest voice or the most senior title."
Amodei told Dimon that he encourages other leaders to demonstrate honesty and trust. He said that every two weeks he holds a "Dario Vision Quest," an all-hands meeting where he said he speaks to the company about what's going on.
Amodei said he tries not to hide things from staff and doesn't rely on corporate jargon. That creates an environment where employees can trust leaders and leaders can trust employees, he said.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
"Everyone feels that we're being honest with them," Amodei said, adding that this carries "enormous value."
Amodei told Dimon that the approach works because employees share the same values and a common goal. Whether the task is training a model, meeting a safety objective, building a product, or advancing a policy priority, "the whole company comes together to make it happen," he said.
Amodei said that maintaining that kind of environment has helped with retention, which is critical given the company's dependence on senior leaders and key technical team members. Amodei said that all seven cofounders, including himself, are still at the company, along with over three-quarters of its first 100 employees. In its IPO filing, Anthropic said it experienced only about 1% "regrettable attrition" in a 12-month period.
Amodei added that it's a "relatively frequent" occurrence for employees to come back after leaving. He said two major product employees left and came back after two weeks.
"They said, 'Sorry, we didn't appreciate what we had,'" Amodei said about their return.

STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours.
Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines.
The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO).
SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear.
A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights.
Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds.
"We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment."
Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28.
Ship carried 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which were deployed into LEO on schedule today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch.
The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO. The addition of this new set of V3s will add a terabit of data capacity to the constellation, according to SpaceX's Flight 15 mission outline . That's equivalent to the amount contributed by 10 Starlink V2 launches, which are carried out by SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket.
Three of the V3 Starlinks flying today were equipped with cameras to point back at Ship after deployment in order to analyze its heatshield tiles and other hardware following its ascent to orbit. Their data will help SpaceX determine if Ship can indeed come home to Starbase on Saturday.
"Starship will only execute a return to launch site if the flight control team has ensured that the vehicle systems critical for reentry maneuvers and final landing burn and tower approach are healthy," SpaceX wrote in its Flight 15 mission description.
SpaceX engineers will have ample time to go over Ship's systems before making a final landing decision. Ship is scheduled to circle Earth 14 times, spending more than 21 hours in space before coming home.
You can follow all of the action on here at Space.com via our Flight 15 live updates page .
SpaceX has reserved three contingency checkpoints during Flight 15's mission timeline to allow for an early Pacific Ocean return, should engineers determine a catch attempt to be unfeasible or unwise. The first comes just 10 minutes after the completion of Starlink satellite deployment, the second at T+7 hours and 15 minutes, and a final one at T+20 hours and 41 minutes.
Should Ship continue to look good through each of these milestones, SpaceX will proceed with a 10-second deorbit burn at approximately T+21 hours and 36 minutes, setting the spacecraft on a trajectory back toward South Texas. Its plunge through Earth's atmosphere will begin about 35 minutes later. SpaceX has also designated a contingency splashdown zone in the Gulf of Mexico, should conditions prevent a safe catch during Ship's final approach.
If all goes according to plan, Ship will return to Starbase on Saturday at approximately 4:17 p.m. EST (2117 GMT; 3:17 p.m. Texas time), about 22.5 hours after liftoff. A successful catch would be a major milestone for SpaceX — the first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage.
Full reusability is central to the company's ambitions for launching its V3 Starlink satellites, as well as a proposed constellation of orbital data centers envisioned by company founder and CEO Elon Musk . The next-gen Starlink constellation will consist of about 100,000 satellites, while the AI network will be 10 times that size, Musk has said. Building and maintaining those constellations will require a mind-boggling number of launches. Indeed, SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship liftoffs per year by 2030 , according to Musk.
Some of Starship's other planned missions won't necessarily require full reusability, but the spacecraft's reliability will be critical to NASA's Artemis program and its efforts to return astronauts to the moon . The space agency selected Starship as one of the program's crewed lunar landers, and it's slated to fly a demonstration mission with NASA's Orion spacecraft and Artemis III astronauts to Earth orbit in the summer of 2027.
Editor's note: This story was updated at 7:10 p.m. ET on Nov. 13 with news of successful payload deployment.
Josh Dinner is Space.com's Spaceflight Staff Writer and a photographer with a passion for science and exploration. He has worked the space beat since 2016, covering the evolution of NASA's commercial spaceflight partnerships and crewed missions, planetary science missions, the Artemis program and humanity's return to the moon. He also enjoys building 1:144-scale model rockets and spacecraft. Find some of Josh's launch photography on Instagram , and follow him on X , where he mostly posts in haiku.

articles.content_orig:
Flight 15 expected to orbit Earth about 14 times over 22 hours, before company catches it at Starbase, Texas
SpaceX’s Starship megarocket blasted off from Texas on Friday afternoon, as the aerospace company sought to make history with a double catch of its reusable rocket.
Starship Flight 15 is expected to orbit the Earth about 14 times over the course of 22 hours, before the company catches the rocket at its launchpad at Starbase, in south Texas .
The rocket itself was composed of two elements: the lower booster, with 33 raptor engines that fired off during takeoff, and the Starship at the top.
SpaceX had planned for both components to return to its tower, but the booster, named Super Heavy, was aborted and splashed down in the sea. The cause of that diversion remains unknown.
The Starship continued on sailing through space.
SpaceX has launched a flurry of test flights in recent years, as its chief executive Elon Musk pushes his vision of taking humans into space.

articles.title_orig: CJP: India’s protesters face government crackdown after summer victory
articles.title_zh: CJP: India’s protesters face government crackdown after summer victory
articles.content_orig:
Cheers erupted at Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site in July as news broke that Gen-Z protests had forced federal education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign.
One protester turned to me, beaming: "This is the youth's victory."
Just over three months later, the mood has shifted dramatically. Student protesters are now struggling even to assemble. Demonstrations by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) last month over voting rights were met with sweeping restrictions and thousands of peaceful protesters were detained .
The summer had seen a new wave of dissent in India, driven by deep frustration among the youth and fuelled by irreverent online satire.
The movement spread across the country, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a leader with a strongman image, unaccustomed to open criticism or mockery, struggled to contain it. But the government's increasingly forceful security response suggests it has learned from its rare concession to protesters, invoking public order to curb dissent.
The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national spokesperson Syed Zafar Islam rejected accusations of heavy-handedness and told the BBC: "The right to protest and freedom of expression is mandated by the constitution, but it has to be done within the law. It cannot override the rights of others, at the cost of public security".
This is by no means the first time the Modi government has faced large-scale protests.
But the breadth of them pose a challenge for the BJP, according to Yamini Aiyar, former president of the Centre for Policy Research and visiting professor at Brown University.
"They are not defined by caste, gender or economic class," Aiyar said. "Even some of the core BJP base, the upwardly mobile, lower-income classes, were attracted by the movement."
The scale of the youth protests is also magnified by its online presence. Protesters have broken a longstanding political taboo, openly mocking the prime minister online.
"It's more than just laughs," said Sakhi, a student protester who identifies as they/them and affiliated with one of Delhi University's left-wing student organisations.
"The fear of repercussions in other generations isn't felt as much in ours," they said. "Comedy is a new language to challenge authority."
Previous protest movements posed serious challenges to Modi but were easier to dismiss as representing narrow sections of society or to label "anti-national", according to Aiyar.
In 2020, farmers protesting against controversial agricultural reforms were blocked from entering Delhi, leading to months of demonstrations and, at times, clashes on the capital's borders. After a year of protests, the government abandoned the reforms.
Protests against a contentious citizenship law in 2019 and 2020 are a stark reminder of the powers of the judiciary should anyone be deemed a national security threat.
Student activist Umar Khalid was arrested under anti-terror laws after violent clashes in Delhi that killed 53 people, mostly Muslims. He was accused of being a "key conspirator". He has now spent more than six years in jail without his trial having begun.
His partner Banojyotsna Lahiri told the BBC they have no regrets, but that the situation instilled "a kind of fear that has prevailed".
"We are just looking at a very dark mesh of empty space, because we don't know when the endpoint is," Lahiri said. Khalid's latest appeal was lodged this month.
Aiyar believes opponents are using a familiar "playbook" today to "de-legitimise" protests, but that it isn't resonating as convincingly.
Nevertheless, the youth protests have struggled to recapture this summer's momentum.
CJP leaders, including spokesperson Saurav Das, have faced repeated detentions and legal action. Das and fellow leader Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in Delhi's Tihar jail after being accused of trespassing at Jantar Mantar.
The site of their summer victory has since been struck off the list of authorised protest venues, a decision being challenged in court.
Protesters from other groups, including the left-wing All India Students' Association (Aisa), have also faced police action over allegations of defying orders.
"We were expecting some kind of crackdown," said Das. He added that "the government has learnt a lot" since the summer.
Legal experts warn the proceedings themselves can have a chilling effect.
"A lot of cases can lead to acquittals, but it can take years. The process is the punishment, and that can deter protesters," said Ali Khan, an assistant professor at Lloyd Law College.
The restrictions on demonstrations have become excessive, according to constitutional lawyer Vrinda Grover, who is advising the CJP.
"Those who are organising the protests have repeatedly emphasised that this is non-violent," she argued. "Rights have been whittled down in the name of law and order."
The BJP has rejected suggestions it is suppressing peaceful dissent.
Islam told the BBC that demonstrations "cannot override the rights of other citizens just because a handful of people want to protest and be responsible for violence".
Even dissenting online carries risk. Sakhi's viral social media posts have attracted targeted abuse and transphobic attacks. The BBC has seen posts threatening them with violence and rape.
Sometimes, it can deter Sakhi from protesting or even make them change the way they dress.
"Making people laugh can turn into being called anti-national," Sakhi said. "They want me to feel damaged," they added.
They claim some of their content was removed after getting millions of views.
Under India's information technology laws, the government can order platforms to block content on national security grounds. Notices on X and Instagram have shown accounts being withheld in India.
CJP leaders have likened the crackdown to the 1975 Emergency, when then prime minister Indira Gandhi suspended civil liberties and jailed political opponents.
Yet dissent has not been stamped out.
Opposition parties have, in part, filled the void. Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi on 1 November for a rally organised by INDIA bloc , an alliance of opposition parties led by Congress, and permitted by the authorities.
CJP leaders, meanwhile, insist the movement is bigger than their organisation.
When Das walked out Delhi's Tihar prison on 21 October, photographs showed him smiling.
"I would just say wait and watch," Das told us. "Time is on our side. We are a very young generation."
